candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items); this item tests client advocacy, advance-care/goals-of-care communication, ethical decision support, and collaboration with surrogate decision-makers.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Client advocacy and shared goals-of-care decision support when the client lacks capacity
candidate.educational_objective: Support surrogate goals-of-care decisions after severe traumatic brain injury by communicating prognostic uncertainty honestly, avoiding premature nihilism, and centering the client's known values and prior wishes.

options.A: Support careful clinician-family discussion that acknowledges prognostic uncertainty and considers the client's known values, prior wishes, and all available clinical evidence
options.B: Tell the family that an unfavorable long-term outcome can be determined reliably from ultra-early injury findings alone during the first days
options.C: Avoid goals-of-care discussion unless the client previously completed a formal written advance directive
options.D: Recommend withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment whenever the client remains unconscious after the initial resuscitation period

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The current Neurocritical Care Society guideline for neuroprognostication after moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury is intended to support counseling of surrogate decision-makers. It recommends that prognostication be performed carefully, acknowledge uncertainty, avoid nihilism, and consider all available evidence. It also recommends against basing prognosis only on ultra-early injury characteristics in the first 3 days and recognizes the importance of documented or inferred patient wishes when treatment decisions are considered. B and D overstate early prognostic certainty and can drive self-fulfilling treatment limitation. C is incorrect because surrogate decision-making and goals-of-care communication remain necessary when a client lacks capacity even if no written directive exists.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current NCS guidance directly supports cautious, uncertainty-aware neuroprognostication and surrogate counseling that avoids premature treatment limitation based on ultra-early findings and considers the patient's values and wishes.
candidate.source_document_title: Guidelines for Neuroprognostication in Critically Ill Adults with Moderate–Severe Traumatic Brain Injury
candidate.source_locator: NCS guideline → 'How to Use These Guidelines' and Good Practice Recommendations: guideline supports clinicians counseling families/surrogates; prognostication should not be based only on ultra-early injury characteristics in the first 3 days; unless irreversible brain-stem damage or documented predetermined wishes apply, provide a period of full support before attempting definitive neuroprognostication; prognostication should acknowledge uncertainty, avoid nihilism, consider all available evidence, and not rely on anecdote alone. Values/preferences discussion notes that goals-of-care decisions should align with patient wishes as best understood by surrogates.
candidate.source_version_date: NCS evidence-based guideline released February 2024; currently listed in the NCS guideline library and accessed 2026-08-18
candidate.stem: A client with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury lacks decision-making capacity, and the family asks whether life-sustaining treatment should be limited because recovery appears uncertain early in the course. Which nursing approach best supports appropriate goals-of-care decision-making?
